prompt: Adobe XD is mainly used for:
options: Designing and prototyping user interfaces for websites and apps
Editing and colour grading videos for social media
explanation: XD is a UI/UX design and prototyping tool.

prompt: Why use a UI tool like XD instead of Photoshop for app screens?
options: It's built for layouts, components and clickable prototypes
XD has more advanced photo retouching tools than Photoshop
explanation: Photoshop excels at image editing; XD is built for interface design.

prompt: In Adobe XD, a single screen of your design lives on:
explanation: Artboards represent screens or pages.

prompt: When creating a new XD file, you can choose a preset size such as:
explanation: Presets match common device screen sizes.

prompt: In XD, which mode lets you switch from designing to linking screens?
explanation: XD has Design, Prototype and Share modes.

prompt: The Layers panel in XD helps you:
options: See and organise every element on an artboard
Run and test the code behind your design
explanation: Layers show structure and stacking order.

prompt: The Property Inspector on the right side of XD shows:
options: The project's version history and comments from reviewers
Settings for the selected element, such as size, colour and border
explanation: It's where you adjust properties.

prompt: To select a layer inside a group directly in XD, you can:
options: Ungroup everything and delete the group first
Double-click into the group or Cmd/Ctrl-click the element
explanation: Direct selection avoids ungrouping.

prompt: Bringing assets from Photoshop or Illustrator into XD lets you:
options: Reuse existing artwork in your UI designs
Convert your whole design into a single flat image
explanation: XD can import and paste content from other Adobe apps.

prompt: Saving as a cloud document in XD allows you to:
options: Access your file across devices and share it easily
Lock the file so no one, including you, can edit it
explanation: Cloud documents sync and support collaboration.

prompt: Why learn a tool's quirks early?
options: It saves time and frustration when something behaves unexpectedly
Quirks only appear when you export to PDF
explanation: Knowing limitations helps you work around them.

prompt: The best way to learn a design tool is to:
options: Wait for a project at work
Follow along and practise each technique yourself
explanation: Hands-on practice builds skill.

prompt: UI design is mainly concerned with:
options: How an interface looks and how its elements are arranged
How the server stores and processes user data
explanation: UI covers visual design and layout.

prompt: Which task suits Photoshop better than XD?
options: Linking app screens into a prototype
explanation: Photoshop is a photo editor.

prompt: An artboard sized 375 × 812 is most likely designed for:
explanation: That's a common iPhone viewport size.

prompt: What are XD's three main workspaces?
explanation: You design, wire interactions, then share.

prompt: Renaming layers clearly in a design file helps:
options: You and developers find elements quickly
Make the exported file size much smaller
explanation: Organised layers make handoff easier.

prompt: A logo was made in Illustrator. The simplest way to use it in an XD design is:
options: Copy and paste or import it as a vector
Take a phone photo of the screen
explanation: XD accepts vector content from Illustrator.

prompt: Why are cloud documents useful for teams?
options: Everyone works from the latest version
explanation: Cloud files reduce version confusion.

prompt: If a feature in your design tool behaves strangely, a good first step is:
options: Check the tool's documentation or community for known issues
explanation: Many quirks have known workarounds.

prompt: In XD, how do you round the corners of a rectangle?
options: Drag the corner handles or set the corner radius in the Property Inspector
Apply a drop shadow and increase its blur
Use the Pen tool to redraw each corner as a curve
explanation: Corner radius controls rounded corners.

prompt: Holding Shift while drawing an ellipse creates:
explanation: Shift constrains proportions.

prompt: Combining two shapes into one using union, subtract, intersect or exclude is called:
explanation: Boolean operations build complex shapes from simple ones.

prompt: The Pen tool is used to:
options: Draw custom paths and shapes point by point
explanation: Click to make straight lines; drag to make curves.

prompt: A linear gradient:
options: Blends colours along a straight line
Blends from a centre point outward
explanation: Radial gradients blend outwards from a centre.

prompt: A layout grid helps designers:
options: Align content consistently across a design
explanation: Grids create order and rhythm.

prompt: Smart guides in XD:
options: Remove hidden layers from the file
Appear automatically to show alignment and spacing
explanation: They help you place elements precisely.

prompt: The alignment tools help you:
options: Change the font of selected text
Line up elements by their edges or centres
explanation: Align left, centre, right, top, middle, bottom.

prompt: 'Distribute horizontally' makes elements:
options: Evenly spaced from left to right
explanation: Distribution equalises gaps.

prompt: Point text and area text in XD differ because:
options: Area text wraps within a fixed box
explanation: Click once for point text; drag a box for area text.

prompt: The easiest way to place a photo inside a shape in XD is:
options: Trace the photo with the Pen tool
Drag the image onto the shape to fill it
explanation: XD masks the image to the shape.

prompt: A mask in design software:
options: Permanently deletes the parts of the image you don't need
Shows part of an image through a shape and hides the rest
explanation: Masks are non-destructive.

prompt: Which shape tool would you use for a circular profile picture frame?
explanation: Hold Shift for a perfect circle.

prompt: A button with rounded corners is created by:
options: Drawing four lines and curving them by hand
explanation: Rounded rectangles are common in UI.

prompt: To cut a circle out of a square in XD, use:
explanation: Subtract removes the top shape from the one below.

prompt: Clicking and dragging with the Pen tool creates:
explanation: Dragging pulls out curve handles.

prompt: Why should UI designers check colour contrast?
options: So text and controls are readable for everyone, including people with low vision
So the design uses as many brand colours as possible
explanation: Good contrast is essential for accessibility.

prompt: An 8-point spacing system means:
options: Spacing values are multiples of 8, like 8, 16, 24
Every screen uses exactly eight colours
explanation: Consistent spacing makes layouts feel orderly.

prompt: You want three cards evenly spaced across a row. Which tool helps most?
explanation: Distribution equalises gaps between objects.

prompt: For a long product description that should wrap neatly, use:
explanation: Area text wraps inside its box.

prompt: Large, unoptimised images in a design can cause:
explanation: Optimise images for performance.

prompt: Why are masks described as non-destructive?
options: The hidden parts of the image are kept and can be revealed later
They merge every layer into one image
explanation: You can adjust the mask anytime.

prompt: PNG is a good export format when you need:
options: The smallest possible file for large photos
Transparency and sharp edges, such as icons
explanation: PNG supports transparency and is lossless.

prompt: Exporting at 2x or 3x is used for:
options: Making files two or three times smaller
explanation: Higher multiples keep images crisp on dense screens.

prompt: Sharing a design for review in XD gives stakeholders:
options: A link where they can view and comment
explanation: Review links collect feedback.

prompt: Saving a design presentation as a PDF is useful because:
options: Almost anyone can open it without design software
explanation: PDFs are universal.

prompt: 'Share for development' in XD provides developers with:
options: Measurements, colours, fonts and downloadable assets
The finished, working code for the app
explanation: Design specs support accurate builds.

prompt: Compressing images before publishing helps:
explanation: Smaller images improve performance.

prompt: JPG is usually best for:
explanation: JPG compresses photos well but has no transparency.

prompt: Lossy compression:
options: Reduces file size by discarding some data
explanation: JPG is lossy; PNG is lossless.

prompt: Why mark assets for export in a design file?
options: To stop anyone else from seeing them
So developers can download exactly the images they need
explanation: Marked assets appear in the developer handoff.

prompt: When asking for feedback on a design, you should:
options: Ask only whether they like it or not
Explain the goal and the specific questions you want answered
explanation: Focused questions get useful feedback.

prompt: A presentation PDF of your screens is useful for:
options: Showing designs to clients who don't use XD
explanation: It's a simple way to share static screens.

prompt: SVG is a good format for:
options: Icons and logos that must scale without losing quality
explanation: SVG is a vector format.

prompt: Which export format should you use for an app icon with a transparent background?
explanation: PNG keeps transparency.

prompt: A share link set to 'comments allowed' lets reviewers:
options: Leave feedback pinned to parts of the design
explanation: Comments keep feedback in context.

prompt: Design handoff is:
options: Passing designs and specifications to developers to build
Sending the design to the client for payment
explanation: Clear handoff prevents mistakes.

prompt: Which action improves a website's loading speed most directly?
explanation: Images are often the heaviest assets.

prompt: Why export assets at multiple resolutions?
options: Different screens have different pixel densities
explanation: 1x, 2x and 3x cover common devices.

prompt: A client wants to see your screens on a laptop without any design software. Send:
options: A PDF or a share link
explanation: PDFs and links open anywhere.

prompt: Repeat Grid in XD lets you:
options: Duplicate an element into rows or columns and edit them all at once
Repeat the same animation on every screen
explanation: Great for lists and card grids.

prompt: Dropping a text file onto a Repeat Grid text element will:
options: Fill each item with a line from the file
Replace every item with the same first line
explanation: Fast way to add realistic content.

prompt: Dragging several images onto a Repeat Grid image shape:
options: Fills each item with a different image
explanation: XD distributes the images across the grid.

prompt: A component in XD is:
options: An export preset that saves assets as PNG files
A single-use shape that can't be reused
A reusable element where changes to the main component update all instances
explanation: Components keep designs consistent.

prompt: Component states allow a button to have:
options: Different looks such as default, hover and pressed
explanation: States show interaction variations.

prompt: A style guide documents:
options: Colours, typography, spacing and components for a product
The project budget and delivery timeline
explanation: It keeps design consistent.

prompt: Saving colours in the Assets panel helps you:
options: Hide colours you no longer want to use
Reuse and update brand colours consistently
explanation: Change a saved colour once to update everywhere.

prompt: Character styles store:
options: Font, size, weight and spacing settings for text
explanation: Text styles keep typography consistent.

prompt: The Assets panel in XD holds:
explanation: It's your document's design library.

prompt: Linked assets from a shared library mean that:
options: Updates to the library can be pushed to every file using it
Each file has its own separate copy forever
explanation: Libraries keep teams in sync.

prompt: Keeping multiple design versions helps when:
options: You want to compare options or roll back
explanation: Version history protects work.

prompt: Coediting in XD lets:
options: Only one person open a file
Only one person open the file at a time
Several designers work on the same file at the same time
explanation: Real-time collaboration speeds teamwork.

prompt: Which XD feature is best for building a product listing of 12 identical cards quickly?
explanation: Repeat Grid duplicates and keeps items in sync.

prompt: You change the main button component's colour. What happens to its instances?
options: Only the first instance changes colour
They update to match, unless overridden
explanation: That's the power of components.

prompt: Why does a style guide matter as a product grows?
options: It keeps new screens consistent and speeds up design
It's only needed for printed brochures
explanation: Consistency improves usability and efficiency.

prompt: You need every heading in a design to use the same font and size. Use:
explanation: Apply the style to each heading.

prompt: A design team keeps one shared library of components. The main benefit is:
options: Every product uses the same up-to-date elements
Each designer invents their own buttons
explanation: Shared libraries create a single source of truth.

prompt: Before a big redesign, it's wise to:
options: Save a version you can return to
explanation: Versions protect against mistakes.

prompt: Using realistic content in designs (not just 'lorem ipsum') helps because:
options: You see how real text lengths and images affect the layout
It makes the design file load faster
explanation: Real content reveals layout issues.

prompt: Brand colours should be stored as:
options: Random hex codes typed each time
Named swatches in the assets library
explanation: Named swatches are easy to reuse and update.

prompt: What should you define before designing the first web page?
options: The page's purpose, its users and the content it needs
The hosting company and server type
explanation: Purpose and content shape the layout.

prompt: A website header usually contains:
options: The copyright notice and privacy policy links
Logo, main navigation and key actions like search or cart
explanation: Headers help users orient and navigate.

prompt: Social media icons in a design should be:
explanation: Consistency looks professional.

prompt: Setting typography early helps:
options: Avoid using any headings on the page
Create clear hierarchy and consistency across pages
explanation: Type scale defines headings, body and captions.

prompt: A typographic hierarchy uses differences in:
options: Size, weight and spacing to show importance
explanation: Hierarchy guides the reader's eye.

prompt: A search bar on an online shop should be:
options: Easy to find, usually near the top
explanation: Users expect search near the top.

prompt: Product cards in a grid should show:
options: Image, name, price and a clear action
explanation: Key decision information at a glance.

prompt: Pagination helps users:
options: Log in and reset their password
Move through long lists of content in pages
explanation: Pagination breaks long lists into manageable chunks.

prompt: A website footer typically includes:
options: Contact details, secondary links and legal information
The product checkout and payment form
explanation: Footers hold supporting links.

prompt: A product details page must make it easy to:
options: See key information and add the item to the cart
Read the company's full history first
explanation: The page's job is to support the buying decision.

prompt: Why is the logo usually linked to the homepage?
options: Search engines require every logo to be a link
Users expect clicking the logo to take them home
explanation: It's a widely understood web convention.

prompt: Why use a Repeat Grid for product cards?
options: It turns cards into a single flat image
Cards stay identical in layout and are fast to update
explanation: Consistency and speed.

prompt: Which page section is usually seen first by visitors?
options: The header and hero area at the top
explanation: The top of the page creates the first impression.

prompt: How many typefaces should most websites use?
explanation: Too many fonts look messy.

prompt: Why place search prominently on an e-commerce site?
options: Many users arrive knowing what they want to find
explanation: Search speeds up finding products.

prompt: Which is an alternative to pagination for long product lists?
options: Infinite scroll or a 'Load more' button
explanation: Each has trade-offs for usability.

prompt: Where would most users look for a company's contact details on a website?
explanation: Footers commonly hold contact information.

prompt: On a product page, the 'Add to cart' button should be:
options: Highly visible and close to price and options
The same colour as the background
explanation: The primary action must stand out.

prompt: Which approach makes icons look professional?
options: A consistent set with the same style and stroke weight
explanation: Consistency is key.

prompt: A sticky header that stays visible while scrolling helps users:
options: Download pages faster on slow networks
Navigate at any point on a long page
explanation: Navigation stays within reach.

prompt: Responsive design means:
options: Layouts adapt to different screen sizes
The site loads in one second
explanation: One design adapts across devices.

prompt: A breakpoint is:
options: A screen width at which the layout changes
A bug that breaks the layout
explanation: E.g. switching to one column below 768px.

prompt: Why can designers create responsive layouts without coding?
options: Design tools let them plan layouts for each screen size for developers to build
Browsers automatically design every screen size for them
explanation: Designers specify layouts; developers implement them.

prompt: On a mobile homepage, a multi-column desktop grid usually becomes:
explanation: Narrow screens favour stacked content.

prompt: Navigation menus on mobile are often:
options: Collapsed into a menu icon or bottom bar
explanation: Space is limited on phones.

prompt: Touch targets on mobile should be:
options: Large enough to tap easily, around 44–48 pixels
As small as possible to fit more on screen
explanation: Small targets cause mistakes.

prompt: Exploring colour variations of a design helps you:
options: Avoid having to show the client any options
Compare moods and choose what best fits the brand
explanation: Variations support better decisions.

prompt: Changing the typeface in a design variation mainly changes:
options: The page's loading speed and server
The personality and readability of the design
explanation: Typography strongly affects tone.

prompt: A layout variation might change:
options: The arrangement and hierarchy of content
The website's domain name and hosting
explanation: Layout affects scanning and focus.

prompt: Before presenting a design, it helps to explain:
options: The key decisions and why you made them
explanation: Rationale builds confidence in the design.

prompt: 'Mobile-first' design means:
options: Designing the desktop version first, then shrinking it
Designing for small screens first, then enhancing for larger ones
explanation: It forces focus on essential content.

prompt: On mobile, body text should generally be:
options: Around 10px so more text fits on screen
explanation: Small text is hard to read on phones.

prompt: Why is responsive design especially important in Nigeria?
options: Most people browse the web on mobile phones
Most websites in Nigeria are only viewed on desktops
explanation: Mobile is the main way many users go online.

prompt: Which content should appear first on a mobile homepage?
options: The most important message and action
explanation: Prioritise essentials on small screens.

prompt: A 'hamburger' icon usually represents:
explanation: Three lines signal a menu.

prompt: Why create several design variations before choosing one?
options: Comparing options leads to a stronger final decision
explanation: Exploration reduces the risk of settling early.

prompt: When presenting design variations to a client, you should:
options: Explain how each supports the goals, and recommend one
Show them all without any explanation
explanation: Guide the decision with reasoning.

prompt: Designers communicate responsive behaviour to developers by:
options: Providing layouts for key breakpoints with notes
explanation: Breakpoint designs show how layouts adapt.

prompt: Which layout change best improves scanning on a busy product page?
options: Clear sections with strong headings and white space
explanation: White space and hierarchy aid scanning.

prompt: A prototype is used to:
options: Store user data before the app launches
Simulate how users move through a product before it's built
explanation: Prototypes let you test flows early.

prompt: Wiring in XD's Prototype mode means:
options: Connecting an element to a destination artboard
explanation: Drag the blue handle to link screens.

prompt: The 'home' artboard in a prototype is:
options: The screen with the most elements
The screen where the prototype starts
explanation: Set it with the home icon.

prompt: Which is an XD trigger type?
explanation: Triggers include Tap, Drag, Time, Hover and Voice.

prompt: A 'Time' trigger is useful for:
options: Detecting when the user types text
Moving automatically after a delay, like a splash screen
explanation: It fires without user action.

prompt: Easing in animation controls:
options: How the speed changes during a transition
explanation: Ease-in, ease-out and others make motion feel natural.

prompt: Auto-animate in XD:
options: Animates matching layers between two artboards smoothly
Writes the animation code for developers
explanation: Layers with the same name animate between states.

prompt: For auto-animate to work, layers on both artboards should:
explanation: XD matches layers by name.

prompt: A drag trigger with auto-animate can simulate:
explanation: Drag interactions mimic swiping.

prompt: The 'Previous Artboard' action is useful for:
options: Back buttons that return to wherever the user came from
explanation: It avoids wiring many back links manually.

prompt: Overlays in XD are used to show:
options: Menus and pop-ups on top of the current screen
explanation: Overlays keep the background screen visible.

prompt: 'Scroll To' lets a link:
options: Open an external website in the browser
Jump to a section on the same artboard
explanation: Useful for one-page navigation.

prompt: Why test a prototype with users before development?
options: It guarantees the app will succeed after launch
It's much cheaper to fix problems before code is written
explanation: Early testing saves time and money.

prompt: Which action creates a link from a button to another screen in XD?
options: Drag the connector from the button to the target artboard in Prototype mode
Double-click the button in Design mode
Rename the button layer to match the screen name
explanation: Wiring happens in Prototype mode.

prompt: A hover trigger is most relevant for:
explanation: Touch screens don't have hover.

prompt: A transition that starts fast and slows to a stop uses:
explanation: Ease-out decelerates at the end.

prompt: You move a card's position between two artboards with the same layer names and use auto-animate. What happens in the prototype?
options: The card disappears and reappears instantly
The card glides smoothly to its new position
explanation: Auto-animate tweens matching layers.

prompt: A mobile menu that slides over the page is best built with:
explanation: Overlays appear on top of the current screen.

prompt: Why can animations 'not matter' if the basics are wrong?
options: Users can't see animations on most phones
Motion can't fix confusing structure or unclear content
explanation: Get structure and clarity right first.

prompt: Which interaction best mimics swiping through photos on a phone?
options: Time trigger with a dissolve transition
explanation: Drag simulates swipe gestures.

prompt: Good UI animation helps users by:
options: Making screens take longer to load
Showing what changed and where things went
explanation: Motion provides feedback and context.

prompt: Which should you generally avoid animating?
options: Things that slow users down during frequent tasks
Brief feedback when a button is pressed
explanation: Excess motion on repeated actions frustrates users.

prompt: A hover state on a button:
options: Changes its look when the mouse is over it
Plays a sound when the page loads
explanation: Hover states signal interactivity.

prompt: Why give menu items hover states?
options: To show users which item they're about to choose
To make the menu harder to read
explanation: Visual feedback reduces mistakes.

prompt: A search box usually needs which states?
options: Only one state that never changes
Default, hover, focused/active, and showing results
explanation: States show the box is interactive.

prompt: Adding a hover state to items in a Repeat Grid means:
options: Each card shows feedback when hovered
explanation: Components inside grids keep states consistent.

prompt: Stacks in XD let you:
options: Export the design as HTML code
explanation: Stacks keep consistent spacing as you reorder.

prompt: Making navigation work in a prototype means:
options: Removing links so testers stay on one screen
Linking every menu item to its destination screen
explanation: A working nav lets testers explore freely.

prompt: Animation duration for most UI transitions is typically:
explanation: Quick transitions feel responsive.

prompt: Which animation is most helpful?
options: A brief highlight when an item is added to the cart
A 5-second logo spin before every page
explanation: Purposeful motion gives feedback.

prompt: A drop-down showing suggestions under a search box helps users:
options: Find results faster with fewer keystrokes
explanation: Suggestions reduce effort.

prompt: Why use stacks when designing lists?
options: They lock items so they can't be moved
Spacing stays consistent when items are added or moved
explanation: Automatic spacing saves time.

prompt: Which statement about UI animation is true?
options: It should support understanding, not just decorate
explanation: Purpose first.

prompt: On touch devices, what replaces hover feedback?
explanation: Touch screens use press states.

prompt: A focused state on a search field is shown when:
options: The page first loads, before any interaction
The user clicks or taps into it to type
explanation: Focus indicates where input will go.

prompt: Which tool helps add the same hover state to every product card at once?
options: Drawing each hover state by hand with the Pen tool
A component with a hover state inside the Repeat Grid
explanation: Components share states.

prompt: Why should a usability-test prototype have working navigation?
options: It hides navigation problems from testers
Testers can move naturally and reveal real navigation problems
explanation: Realistic prototypes give realistic feedback.

prompt: You add a new item to a stacked list. What happens?
options: The other items shift to keep spacing even
The new item overlaps the others
explanation: Stacks manage spacing automatically.

prompt: What's the difference between UI and UX?
options: UX is the visual style; UI is the user research
UI is how the interface looks; UX is how the whole experience works and feels
explanation: UX covers usefulness, ease and satisfaction.

prompt: Why is bad UX expensive?
options: It makes servers and hosting more expensive
Confused users abandon tasks, and fixing issues after launch costs more
explanation: Lost sales and rework add up.

prompt: Icons work best when:
options: They are unique and never paired with text labels
They are familiar and paired with labels where meaning could be unclear
explanation: Unlabelled icons often confuse users.

prompt: A primary button should:
options: Stand out more than secondary actions
Look the same as every other button
explanation: Visual priority guides users to the main action.

prompt: Button labels like 'Buy now' or 'Create account' are better than 'Submit' because:
options: They tell users exactly what will happen
explanation: Specific labels reduce uncertainty.

prompt: A good form design practice is:
options: Ask only for information you truly need
explanation: Fewer fields mean more completions.

prompt: Form error messages should:
options: Appear only after the user leaves the page
Explain what went wrong and how to fix it, near the field
explanation: Helpful, specific errors reduce frustration.

prompt: A 'vague action' is a problem because:
options: Users can't predict what a button or link will do
It makes the button too colourful
explanation: Clear actions build confidence.

prompt: Visual hierarchy helps users:
options: Know what to look at first and what matters most
explanation: Size, contrast and position signal importance.

prompt: Why can 'fake' placeholder content mislead a design?
options: Real content may be longer or messier and break the layout
Placeholder text is not allowed in prototypes
explanation: Design with realistic content.

prompt: UX design starts with:
options: Choosing colours and fonts for the brand
explanation: User understanding drives good experiences.

prompt: Which technique creates hierarchy?
options: Making headings larger and bolder than body text
Using the same size for everything
explanation: Contrast in size and weight signals importance.

prompt: Which question is mainly a UX question?
options: Which shade of blue looks best?
Can users complete checkout quickly without confusion?
What font size is the logo?
explanation: UX focuses on the overall experience and task success.

prompt: An online shop's checkout is confusing and many users abandon their carts. This shows:
explanation: Friction loses sales.

prompt: Which icon is most universally understood?
explanation: Familiar icons need little explanation.

prompt: A form has 'Cancel' and 'Save' buttons. Which should be visually stronger?
explanation: Emphasise the likely next step.

prompt: Which form improvement usually increases sign-ups?
explanation: Shorter forms convert better.

prompt: Which label is clearest for a button that sends payment?
explanation: Specific labels set expectations.

prompt: On a landing page, what should usually be most prominent?
options: The copyright notice and legal links
The main headline and primary call to action
explanation: Hierarchy guides users to the key message and action.

prompt: Testing a layout with a very long product name helps you:
options: Find out whether the design handles real-world content
explanation: Edge cases reveal layout issues.

prompt: Usability testing means:
options: Asking your team if they like it
Watching real users try to complete tasks with your design
Asking teammates whether they like the colours
explanation: Observation reveals real problems.

prompt: After finishing this programme, a strong next step for a UI/UX designer is:
options: Collect certificates without building any projects
Build a portfolio of case studies showing your process
explanation: Case studies show how you think and solve problems.

prompt: Which tool skills transfer most easily from Adobe XD?
options: Nothing, because every design tool works completely differently
Components, auto layout and prototyping concepts used in Figma and other tools
explanation: Core UI concepts are shared across modern tools.

prompt: Your first XD design should start with:
options: Choosing an artboard size for the target device
explanation: The artboard defines the canvas for your screen.

prompt: Why do designers use a column grid on web layouts?
options: It adds colour and texture to the background
It creates consistent alignment and makes responsive adaptation easier
explanation: Grids give structure that scales across breakpoints.

prompt: Which detail should developers be able to get from a design handoff?
options: The client's payment details and invoice
Exact spacing, font sizes and colour values
explanation: Specs prevent guesswork in the build.

prompt: Overriding a component instance means:
options: Changing every instance of the component at once
Changing that one instance without affecting the main component
explanation: Overrides allow local variations.

prompt: Which information on a product card most helps a shopper decide quickly?
options: A clear image, name and price
explanation: Key decision details belong on the card.

prompt: A layout that shows 4 columns on desktop, 2 on tablet and 1 on mobile is an example of:
options: A fixed-width layout for all screens
explanation: Columns adapt to screen width.

prompt: Which XD feature creates smooth movement between two screens without manual keyframes?
explanation: Auto-animate tweens matching layers.

prompt: Respecting users who prefer reduced motion means:
options: Adding more animation to keep them engaged
Keeping essential animations subtle or optional
explanation: Some users experience discomfort from motion.

prompt: Placing form labels above input fields generally:
explanation: Top-aligned labels are easy to scan.

prompt: When is fixing a UX problem cheapest?
explanation: Changes in design cost far less than in code.

prompt: This course teaches Figma after Adobe XD. What carries over most directly from XD to Figma?
options: Nothing at all, the tools share no ideas
Only the keyboard shortcuts, which are identical
Artboard-style screens, components and prototyping ideas
explanation: Both are interface design tools, so the core ideas transfer even where the buttons differ.

prompt: Why do so many product teams use Figma?
options: It only works offline on one computer
It replaces the need for developers
It is a video editing tool
Several people can design in the same file at the same time
explanation: Figma is browser-based and multiplayer, which suits teams.

prompt: Good interface design starts with:
options: Understanding who the users are and what they need
Adding as many features as possible
explanation: Design serves people, so needs come first.

prompt: Visual hierarchy in a design means:
options: Every element looks exactly the same
Size, weight and colour show what matters most first
Text is always placed at the bottom
explanation: Hierarchy guides the eye in order of importance.

prompt: The design principle of proximity says that:
options: All items must be spaced equally far apart
Buttons must touch the screen edge
Related items should sit close together
Images should never sit near text
explanation: Grouping by distance tells users what belongs together.

prompt: Why is white space (negative space) valuable?
options: It is wasted space that should be filled
It gives content room and makes it easier to scan
explanation: Space reduces clutter and improves focus.

prompt: Contrast between text and its background mainly affects:
options: How easily people can read it
The file size of the design
How many pages the file has
explanation: Low contrast is hard to read, especially for low-vision users.

prompt: Lining elements up along shared edges is the principle of:
explanation: Alignment creates order and a tidy layout.

prompt: Repeating the same button style throughout an app supports:
options: Consistency, so users learn the pattern once
explanation: Consistent patterns reduce what users must relearn.

prompt: A persona is:
options: A realistic profile of a typical user, based on research
explanation: Personas keep design decisions focused on real users.

prompt: Focusing on user needs means designing around:
options: The goals and problems of the people using the product
explanation: User-centred design solves real problems.

prompt: A simple way to learn what users need is to:
options: Talk to them and watch them use the product
explanation: Interviews and observation reveal real needs.

prompt: True or false: users always describe exactly what they need without any research.
explanation: People often struggle to express needs, so observation and testing matter.

prompt: Iteration in design means:
options: Designing once and never changing it
Duplicating the same frame many times
Improving a design in repeated rounds of feedback and changes
explanation: Each round gets the design closer to what users need.

prompt: After testing a first version and finding problems, a designer should:
options: Refine the design and test again
explanation: Test, learn and refine is the iteration loop.

prompt: Why make quick low-detail versions early on?
options: They are cheap to change while ideas are still forming
They look best in a portfolio
explanation: Low-fidelity work invites fast change.

prompt: Figma runs:
options: Only on a single offline Windows PC
In a web browser and in a desktop app
explanation: Figma is cloud-based, with a desktop app as an option.

prompt: Where are Figma files saved by default?
options: In the cloud, so they sync automatically
explanation: Cloud saving means no manual Save button is needed.

prompt: True or false: Figma files update for everyone with access as changes are made.
explanation: Changes sync in real time to collaborators.

prompt: To start using Figma you first need to:
explanation: A free account gives access to the editor.

prompt: Figma's free plan is a good starting point because it:
options: Lets you learn the full editor without paying
explanation: Beginners can practise on the free plan.

prompt: The Figma file browser (starter screen) is where you:
options: Edit vector paths and anchor points
See recent files, drafts and projects, and start new ones
explanation: It is the home screen before opening a file.

prompt: Files you create before putting them in a team project usually sit in:
explanation: Drafts hold your personal files.

prompt: In the Figma editor, the left sidebar mainly shows:
explanation: Layers and pages live on the left.

prompt: The right sidebar in Figma shows:
options: Design, Prototype and inspect properties for the selection
A list of every Figma user
A list of everyone who uses Figma worldwide
explanation: Properties change with what is selected.

prompt: The large open area in the middle of the Figma editor is called the:
explanation: You design on the infinite canvas.

prompt: A Figma file can hold several:
options: Pages, each with its own canvas
explanation: Pages help organise large files.

prompt: A downloaded .fig project file is opened in Figma by:
options: Importing it into the file browser
explanation: Import or drag the .fig file into Figma.

prompt: True or false: you can drag a .fig file onto the Figma file browser to import it.
explanation: Drag and drop is one way to import project files.

prompt: Which shortcut temporarily lets you pan around the Figma canvas?
options: Hold the Space bar and drag
explanation: Space-drag moves the view without moving objects.

prompt: In Figma, Shift + 1 is used to:
options: Zoom to fit everything on the canvas
Export the whole file as a PDF
explanation: Shift+1 fits all content in view.

prompt: In Figma, Shift + 2 zooms to:
explanation: Shift+2 zooms to what you have selected.

prompt: The Move tool in Figma uses the shortcut:
explanation: V is the Move tool, as in many design apps.

prompt: What does Figma's Scale tool (K) do differently from a normal resize?
options: It scales strokes, effects and text in proportion
explanation: Scale keeps everything in proportion, not just the box.

prompt: What can a frame do that a group cannot?
options: Have its own fill, clip content and use auto layout
Be renamed in the layers panel
explanation: Frames are containers with their own properties; groups just wrap layers.

prompt: In Figma, the Frame tool shortcut is:
explanation: F or A draws a frame.

prompt: Constraints such as left, right or scale apply to layers inside a:
explanation: Constraints are set relative to the parent frame.

prompt: Ctrl/Cmd + G in Figma:
explanation: G groups; Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+G frames the selection.

prompt: The slice tool (S) in Figma is used to:
options: Cut a shape into pieces permanently
Mark an exact area of the canvas to export
explanation: Slices define export regions.

prompt: Sections (Shift + S) in Figma help you:
options: Group frames on the canvas into labelled areas
explanation: Sections organise the canvas, such as by flow or status.

prompt: Which shortcut draws a rectangle in Figma?
explanation: R is the Rectangle tool.

prompt: To give only the top two corners of a rectangle rounded corners, you:
options: Use the independent corner radius setting
explanation: Each corner can have its own radius.

prompt: Holding Shift while drawing a rectangle gives you:
explanation: Shift locks the proportions.

prompt: In Figma, L draws a line and Shift + L draws:
explanation: Shift+L is the Arrow tool.

prompt: The Ellipse tool in Figma uses the shortcut:
explanation: O draws ellipses and circles.

prompt: Figma's ellipse arc settings make it easy to draw:
explanation: Sweep and ratio settings turn circles into arcs and rings.

prompt: A new polygon in Figma starts with how many sides by default?
explanation: The default polygon is a triangle; you can change the count.

prompt: With the Star tool you can adjust the number of points and the:
options: Font size of any text inside it
Ratio, which controls how deep the points go
explanation: Ratio changes how spiky the star is.

prompt: Clicking an image fill in Figma lets you change its mode to:
explanation: Image fills have scaling modes.

prompt: Figma's image fill settings let you adjust:
explanation: Basic image adjustments are built in.

prompt: The Multiply blend mode in Figma generally makes the result:
explanation: Multiply darkens; Screen lightens.

prompt: The Screen blend mode generally makes the result:
explanation: Screen is the opposite of Multiply.

prompt: Saving a colour as a style in Figma means:
options: It only works on text layers, never shapes
You can reuse it and update it everywhere at once
explanation: Styles keep colours consistent.

prompt: Which is NOT a gradient type in Figma?
explanation: Figma offers linear, radial, angular and diamond.

prompt: A linear gradient blends colours:
options: Outward from the centre in a circle
Along a straight line from one point to another
Around a centre point like a clock
explanation: Radial goes outward; angular goes around.

prompt: When you use a layer as a mask in Figma, the mask layer must be:
options: Below the layers it should clip
explanation: The bottom layer of the group becomes the mask.

prompt: A common use of a mask in Figma is to:
options: Show a photo only inside a circle shape
explanation: Masks crop content to a shape.

prompt: Boolean Subtract in Figma:
options: Removes the top shape from the bottom shape
explanation: Subtract cuts away using the top shape.

prompt: Which boolean operation keeps only the area where shapes overlap?
explanation: Intersect leaves the shared area.

prompt: Boolean Union in Figma:
options: Cuts a hole in a shape
explanation: Union merges shapes.

prompt: The Pen tool shortcut in Figma is:
explanation: P is the Pen tool.

prompt: Figma's vector networks let a single point:
options: Connect to more than two lines
explanation: Unlike classic paths, Figma points can branch.

prompt: Clicking and dragging while placing a pen point creates:
explanation: Dragging pulls out Bézier handles.

prompt: The Pencil tool (Shift + P) is best for:
explanation: Pencil draws freeform strokes.

prompt: Figma's alignment buttons let you:
options: Line up selected layers by edges or centres
explanation: Align left, centre, right, top, middle and bottom.

prompt: Tidy up in Figma is used to:
options: Space selected items evenly in a neat grid
explanation: Tidy up distributes items evenly.

prompt: Holding Alt/Option while hovering over another layer shows:
options: The total file size in megabytes
The distance between the selected layer and that layer
explanation: This is a quick way to measure spacing.

prompt: Line height in Figma's text settings controls:
options: The vertical space between lines of text
explanation: Line height affects readability.

prompt: Letter spacing adjusts:
explanation: Tight or loose tracking changes the feel of text.

prompt: A text box set to Auto width will:
options: Grow wider as you type on one line
explanation: Auto height wraps at a fixed width; auto width keeps growing sideways.

prompt: Figma lets you place a stroke inside, centre or:
explanation: Stroke position changes the shape's visual size.

prompt: To make a dashed border in Figma, you change the stroke's:
options: Style to dashed in the stroke settings
explanation: Stroke settings include dash and gap.

prompt: A subtle drop shadow on a card mainly helps to:
options: Change the font on the card
Make it look raised above the background
explanation: Shadows suggest depth and elevation.

prompt: In a drop shadow, the blur value controls:
options: How soft the shadow's edge is
explanation: More blur means a softer shadow.

prompt: An inner shadow makes an element look:
options: Pressed in or cut into the surface
explanation: Inner shadows sit inside the shape.

prompt: Layer blur in Figma blurs:
options: Only what is behind the layer
explanation: Layer blur softens the layer's own content.

prompt: For background blur to show in Figma, the layer's fill must be:
explanation: You see the blur through a semi-transparent fill, like frosted glass.

prompt: Copy properties (Ctrl/Cmd + Alt + C) lets you:
options: Copy a layer's styling and paste it onto another
Copy the text only, without any styling
explanation: Paste properties with Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+V.

prompt: Auto layout in Figma is mainly used to:
options: Let frames resize and space their contents automatically
Blur the background behind a frame
explanation: Auto layout behaves like flexible boxes.

prompt: The shortcut to add auto layout to a selection is:
explanation: Shift+A wraps the selection in an auto layout frame.

prompt: In auto layout, Hug contents means the frame:
options: Shrinks or grows to fit what is inside it
explanation: Hug follows the content; Fill follows the parent.

prompt: An auto layout button grows when its label gets longer because:
options: The frame is set to hug its text contents
The text has a drop shadow
explanation: This is why buttons are often built with auto layout.

prompt: Auto layout settings include direction, spacing between items and:
explanation: Padding is the space inside the frame's edges.

prompt: A layout grid with columns helps you:
options: Place content consistently across a screen
explanation: Column grids give structure and alignment.

prompt: In a column layout grid, the gutter is:
explanation: Margins are on the outside; gutters are between columns.

prompt: Turning a design into a component in Figma uses:
explanation: This creates a main component.

prompt: When you edit a main component, its instances:
explanation: This is the main benefit of components.

prompt: Changing the text on one instance without changing the main component is called:
explanation: Instances can override content while keeping the link.

prompt: Variants in Figma let you:
options: Record a video walkthrough of the file
Group related versions of a component, such as button states
explanation: Variants hold states like default, hover and disabled.

prompt: Responsive design means a layout:
explanation: Layouts must work on phones, tablets and desktops.

prompt: In Figma, which settings help a layout adapt when a frame is resized?
options: Constraints, auto layout and Fill container
explanation: These control how layers react to resizing.

prompt: Seeing teammates' named cursors in a Figma file is known as:
explanation: Several people can work in one file at once.

prompt: Pressing C in Figma lets you:
options: Add a comment to the canvas
explanation: Comments keep feedback in context.

prompt: Clicking a collaborator's avatar at the top of the file lets you:
options: Follow their view as they work
explanation: This is called observation or spotlight.

prompt: Figma's version history is useful because you can:
options: Restore an earlier state of the file
explanation: Versions are saved automatically, and you can name them.

prompt: Dev Mode in Figma is mainly for:
options: Developers inspecting sizes, spacing and code values
explanation: It surfaces measurements and CSS for handoff.

prompt: In inspect or Dev Mode, a developer can copy:
options: Code snippets such as CSS for a layer
explanation: Code values speed up building.

prompt: When sharing a Figma file, you can give people access to:
explanation: Permissions control what others can do.

prompt: Why share a view-only link with a client?
options: They can see and comment without changing the design
explanation: View access protects the work while inviting feedback.

prompt: Which formats can Figma export?
explanation: Export settings are in the right sidebar.

prompt: Exporting an icon at 2x or 3x is done so it:
explanation: Retina screens need larger pixel versions.

prompt: For simple icons and logos that must scale without blur, the best export is:
explanation: SVG is a vector format.

prompt: Figma plugins are used to:
options: Add extra features, such as stock photos or placeholder text
Turn off automatic saving for the file
explanation: Plugins extend what Figma can do.

prompt: True or false: you can run a plugin without leaving the Figma file.
explanation: Plugins run inside the editor.

prompt: The Figma Community is a place to:
options: Store passwords for your team accounts
Find shared files, plugins and UI kits made by others
explanation: Community resources can be duplicated into your drafts.

prompt: Using a file from the Figma Community usually starts with:
options: Emailing the author for a code
Duplicating it into your own drafts
explanation: Duplicating gives you your own editable copy.

prompt: Publishing a team library lets your team:
options: Reuse the same components and styles across files
Edit any file on the internet
explanation: Libraries keep design systems consistent.

prompt: When a library component is updated and published, files using it:
options: Get a notice to review and accept the update
explanation: Teams choose when to pull updates in.

prompt: Before designing the final project screens, a good first step is to:
options: Understand the brief and plan the sections
explanation: Planning keeps the project focused.

prompt: The first screen area of a landing page, seen without scrolling, is usually called the:
explanation: The hero carries the main message and call to action.

prompt: A landing page's main call-to-action button should be:
options: Easy to spot and clearly worded
The same colour as the background
explanation: A clear CTA drives the action you want.

prompt: Using a column layout grid while building the landing page helps:
options: Keep sections aligned and evenly spaced
explanation: Grids bring order to long pages.

prompt: Reusing components for repeated cards on the landing page means:
options: A change to one card style updates them all
explanation: Components save time and stay consistent.

prompt: Why keep consistent spacing values across landing page sections?
options: It hides mistakes in the code
It is required to save the file
The page feels tidy and professional
explanation: Rhythm in spacing improves quality.

prompt: Turning a desktop design into a mobile design usually means:
options: Stacking content into one column with larger tap targets
explanation: Mobile layouts stack and prioritise.

prompt: Tap targets on mobile should be:
options: As small as possible to save room
Big enough to press easily with a finger
explanation: Small targets cause mis-taps.

prompt: Which frame preset suits a mobile design in Figma?
options: An A4 paper page for printing
A phone frame such as iPhone or Android
explanation: Start with the target device size.

prompt: Design handoff is the step where:
options: The design file is deleted for good
Developers get everything they need to build the design
explanation: Handoff covers specs, assets and behaviour.

prompt: A good handoff includes:
options: Named layers, exported assets and clear specs
explanation: Organised files make building easier.

prompt: Why name layers clearly before handoff?
options: Developers can find and understand each element
It is needed to open Figma
explanation: Messy layer names slow developers down.

prompt: True or false: the final assignment combines skills from the earlier Figma chapters.
explanation: The project brings tools, layout and handoff together.

prompt: In Figma prototyping, the line you drag from one frame to another sets up:
options: A layout grid across the frame
A connection that defines what happens on interaction
A new page in the file
explanation: Connections link a trigger to an action.

prompt: Which is a Figma prototype trigger?
explanation: Triggers include On click, While hovering and After delay.

prompt: Smart animate in Figma animates:
explanation: Layers with the same name move smoothly between frames.

prompt: To show a pop-up on top of the current screen in a Figma prototype, use:
explanation: Overlays appear above the current frame.

prompt: After finishing the Figma chapters, the best way to grow your skills is to:
options: Keep designing real projects and build a portfolio
explanation: Practice and a portfolio turn skills into work.

prompt: In Figma, which design principle is about making the most important element stand out?
explanation: Hierarchy directs attention.

prompt: In Figma, which container clips its contents and can use auto layout?
explanation: Frames clip content; groups do not.

prompt: In Figma, which tool creates precise custom vector shapes point by point?
explanation: The Pen places points with handles.

prompt: In Figma, the copies of a main component placed in a design are called:
explanation: Instances stay linked to the main component.

prompt: In Figma, where do you set up export formats for a selected layer?
options: The layers panel on the left
The Export section of the right sidebar
explanation: Add an export setting and choose a format.
